title: Weighted-average key invariant closes Putnam 2025 B2 (centroid x₁ < x₂)
intent: Prove Putnam 2025 B2 — that the centroid of the region under a strictly increasing, non-negative, continuous curve f on [0,1] lies to the left of the centroid of its solid of revolution (x₁ < x₂) — by carrying the whole proof on one auxiliary inequality, weighted_average_lt_of_strictMono: the f-weighted average of x is strictly less than the f²-weighted average. Two positivity lemmas discharge the centroid formulas' hypotheses, the two centroid lemmas identify x₁ and x₂ with the two sides of that inequality, and one rewrite followed by exact closes the goal.
also_known_as: the one auxiliary statement that carries the idea

parent.name: putnam_2025_b2
parent.statement:
theorem putnam_2025_b2 (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 1, 0 ≤ f x)
  (hfm : StrictMono f)
  (hfc : Continuous f):
  let R : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := { x | 0 ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ x.2 ∧ x.2 ≤ f x.1 }
  let x₁ : ℝ := ⨍ x in R, x.1
  let R' : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) := { x' | ∃ x ∈ R, ∃ θ : ℝ, x'.1 = x.1 ∧ x'.2.1 = x.2 * cos θ ∧ x'.2.2 = x.2 * sin θ }
  let x₂ : ℝ := ⨍ x' in R', x'.1
  x₁ < x₂

children.name: weighted_average_lt_of_strictMono
children.statement:
lemma weighted_average_lt_of_strictMono (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) 1, 0 ≤ f x)
    (hfm : StrictMono f)
    (hfc : Continuous f) :
    (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x * f x) / (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, f x) <
    (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x * f x ^ 2) / (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, f x ^ 2)
children.closed_by: div_lt_div_iff₀ with integral_f_pos and integral_f_sq_pos, then linarith on key_product_ineq f hf hfm hfc
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: For a strictly increasing, non-negative, continuous f, the f-weighted average of x is strictly less than the f^2-weighted average.

children.name: centroid_2d_formula
children.statement:
lemma centroid_2d_formula (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) 1, 0 ≤ f x) (hfc : Continuous f)
    (hI_pos : 0 < ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, f x) :
    let R : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := { p | 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ f p.1 }
    ⨍ p in R, p.1 ∂(volume.prod volume) = (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x * f x) / (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, f x)
children.closed_by: MeasureTheory.setAverage_eq, then h_measure_R (R =ᵐ regionBetween, volume_regionBetween_eq_integral) and h_integral_R (setIntegral_congr_set then setIntegral_fst_regionBetween); ends with smul_eq_mul, inv_mul_eq_div

applicability.goal_shape: A competition problem comparing two derived quantities (here the centroid x₁ of a planar region and the centroid x₂ of its solid of revolution) that both reduce to ratios of the same four single integrals; the comparison becomes a single strict inequality between two weighted averages that a strictly monotone non-negative weight separates.
applicability.use_when: the goal's two sides can both be identified, by formula lemmas, with the two sides of one auxiliary inequality that carries the whole idea (here the f- vs f²-weighted average of x for strictly increasing f ≥ 0); the auxiliary statement is self-contained enough to prove once and cite, and the side conditions on the formulas are discharged by short positivity lemmas. The identification lemmas themselves may be large: in the exemplar centroid_2d_formula (143 lines) and centroid_3d_formula (341 lines) each need their own Fubini / measure-theoretic proof and are most of the file — that is the price of the shape, paid once and walled off behind the two formula lemmas rather than spread through the main proof.
applicability.avoid_when: the auxiliary inequality does not isolate the monotonicity hypothesis that makes the strict comparison true (a merely non-decreasing weight would collapse the comparison); or the denominators' positivity cannot be separated into short lemmas.

consequences: The move obliges the writer to (i) prove the key inequality once (weighted_average_lt_of_strictMono, which itself rests on the heavy key_product_ineq double-integral argument); (ii) prove the two centroid formulas that identify the goal's quantities with the two sides of the inequality (centroid_2d_formula, centroid_3d_formula); and (iii) discharge the positivity hypotheses those formulas need (integral_f_pos, integral_f_sq_pos). Failure mode: the strict inequality x₁ < x₂ holds only because the weight f is strictly increasing; a merely non-decreasing f would collapse the comparison, and a differently shaped region or solid would no longer reduce to the same four single integrals, so the two centroid formulas would not meet the key inequality.
